_comment.source: Atlassian's organization admin REST API v2, from its OpenAPI spec (https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/admin/organization/swagger.json) and reference (https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/admin/organization/rest/api-group-users/). Directory, user and group v2 APIs shipped 2025-11-24 'available to all customers'; the v2 invite API shipped 2026-01-13 for orgs with at least one paid subscription (https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/admin/changelog/). Atlassian only offers SCIM with the Atlassian Guard add-on; none of these endpoints needs Guard.
_comment.credential: An organization API key without scopes, made by an organization admin (admin.atlassian.com, Settings, API keys), sent as a bearer token. A key with scopes, even every accounts, directories and groups scope, gets 403 on invite: these endpoints have no scope yet. It expires when the admin chose (at most a year).
_comment.base_url: The customer's organization: https://api.atlassian.com/admin/v2/orgs/<organization id>, the id in the Atlassian Administration URL.
_comment.directories: Reads use the directory `-`, every directory the key may manage, so an org with several is read as one. Changes need the user's own directory: Atlassian answers 404 to a suspend, restore or removal under `-`. It is read first from the directories the account is in; an account in none or in several gets no change.
_comment.groups: Google groups are pushed as Atlassian groups: a managed group is found by its id, any other by its exact name (two by that name push nothing), and a new one is created in the org's one directory (an org with several gets none). Members are added and removed one at a time in the member's own directory, each read back from the group's member list (GET users filtered by groupIds). Atlassian has no rename, so a group renamed in Google keeps its old name in Atlassian. App roles are given to a pushed group once, in Atlassian.
_comment.settle: Atlassian's single-user read shows the old status for one to two seconds after a suspend or restore, so read-backs are tried again for up to 7.5 seconds.
_comment.membership: `status` is a composite of the account and its org membership: `active` is access, `suspended` and `deactivated` are not. A suspended user keeps their groups and roles and is not billed; restore gives them back. `not_invited` (an Atlassian account with no membership left, such as one removed from the directory) and `for_deletion` are left out: neither has access, and a removal is confirmed by the user no longer being listed with access.
_comment.access: An invite only gives access to what it names, so people are invited into one group, named exactly `appdoorman-users`, which the customer creates and grants the app roles (Jira, Confluence, …) every joiner should have. Its id is looked up by name across every directory; no such group, or more than one, sends nothing. A leaver is suspended (every app, not one product); removing them takes them out of the directory.
_comment.list: The member list uses GET /directories/-/users, which Atlassian deprecated in favour of POST /users/search and keeps working until 2027-06-30. The engine reads lists with GET only, so the Doorkey must move to search before that date. Only claimed (managed) accounts and members of the org are listed: the customer verifies their domain first.
_comment.invites: Unmanaged accounts are listed with their email, before any domain verification. A user invited from the admin UI is listed at once as `active`, so an invite is confirmed at once or fails, never left pending. Atlassian answers 402 'Org does not have any paid products' to an invite on an org without a paid app.

list_joiner_members._comment: The members of the appdoorman-users group, so an invite counts only once the person is in it. Atlassian answers a partly done invite (account made, group not assigned) with 206, a success code; this read-back turns that into a failed change instead of an account without access.
